body_markdown:
Eight historic Hispano Suiza models will be on display at the Circuito de Madring this weekend, along with the brand’s current Carmen Segrera hypercar, as part of a 60-vehicle display at the Spanish Formula 1 Grand Prix. The eight vintage Hispano Suiza models and one current model make Hispano Suiza the most represented brand at the venue.


With deep roots in motorsports, the[historic Hispano Suiza models](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/by-royal-appointment-how-the-kings-of-countries-pop-fashion-art-and-science-fell-for-hispano-suiza/) represent a timeline of the Spanish brand’s racing prowess and engineering innovation. The oldest Hispano Suiza on the field is the 1912 Alfonso XIII, named after the Spanish king who, in addition to being a repeat customer of the brand, competed in several races behind the wheel of a Hispano Suiza. Notably, Alfonso XIII raced in the *Concurso Automovilista del Guadarrama* in Madrid in 1912 in a Hispano Suiza HS 45 HP as well as the Cuesta de las Perdices in 1921. The Alfonso XIII is often described as the first serial-production sports car ever manufactured. A 1922 Hispano Suiza Rabassada will also be on display. It’s a lightweight version of the Alfonso XIII named after the Subida a la Rabassada hillclimb in Barcelona.


Hispano Suiza


The Carmen Sagrera, an electric hypercar which debuted in 2024 to celebrate the brand’s 120th anniversary, represents the brand’s present and future. With more power and racier looks compared to the standard Carmen, the handcrafted Sagrera boasts 1114 horsepower and a 298-mile range. Its zero-to-62 mph time clocks in at just 2.6 seconds, shaving four tenths off the standard Carmen’s time.


If you’re one of those fortunate to be in attendance this weekend and find yourself with some time to kill between track activities, you can see the historic models displayed in the *Marca España* area of Fan Zone E2. The new Carmen Segrera will be displayed alongside other competition-inspired vehicles in Fan Zone A. Our ticket must’ve gotten lost in the mail, but we nevertheless appreciate seeing a healthy gathering of cars from this storied marque celebrated amid the modern F1 cavalcade.
